S2-F024's finding that S1-F009's Kernel 'equilibrium criterion' ('the Kernel owns everything necessary to protect the aggregate invariant, and nothing more') contains an unbound free variable -- 'the aggregate invariant' is unspecified against a law that carries eleven invariants -- so the criterion is a schema, not a decision procedure: its output is entirely determined by which invariant is substituted, and it appears compatible with rival Kernel-size positions only because it is underspecified. Recurs across the S2 kernel-session-2 review series (S2-R-F012 sec.3 shows S1-F012's conjunctive invariant is the maximal, god-object-producing substitution; S2-R-F015 sec8 shows F015's twelve-question sequence is what would have bound the variable; S2-R-F020 sec.4 shows the ADR's derivation rule has the same unbound-invariant limit).

Shown in S2-R-F012 sec8/.3 to be the same rule as S1-F012's 'status assignment, not content transformation', so the two documents' apparent 'transformation' vocabulary dispute is terminological, not substantive. Judged (alongside S1-F005's separation rule and S1-F020's consumption rule) one of the corpus's few reusable pre-implementation exclusion tests -- its function is to reliably produce DO NOT IMPLEMENT verdicts.
